Subject: PO vs Card decisioning - next steps (FinOpsCo)

Hi Sarah and Tom,

Really appreciate the time today — great to learn more about FinOpsCo's rollout plans for your LLM-powered features. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so procurement has what it needs: 

Call recap (high level):
- Pilot: start with 3 months, targeted usage ~5k tokens/day.
- Long-term: production scale could be >$50k/year depending on traffic.
- Key constraints: AP prefers PO for anything over your $50k threshold; pilot customers sometimes run on card or marketplace listing.

What we can provide now:
- Vendor onboarding checklist (attached) — W-9, insurer cert, bank details (stub).
- Draft MSA and pricing summary — I can send via DocuSign or Hub for procurement review.
- Options: marketplace listing (reduces vendor onboarding overhead) OR standard vendor setup with PO + Net30.

Questions / ask for you: 
1) Which commercial path is preferred for the pilot? (card, marketplace, or PO)
2) Timeline for vendor onboarding if we go the PO route?
3) Any required templates (vendor form, tax form) you can send so we pre-fill?

Next steps I propose:
- If pilot on card/marketplace: we send invoice link and enable a smaller test account within 48 hours.
- If PO route: Lauren (cc'd) can lead procurement + legal and we'll prepare the DocuSign MSA + W-9.
- Schedule a 30-min procurement sync next week to align on forms and timeline — please share 2x windows that work.

Attaching: vendor_onboarding_checklist.pdf (stub)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches what we discussed. Quick answers from procurement/ops: 

- Pilot (under $10k): we can usually run on card or a marketplace purchase (marketplace preferred by our finance team because it avoids vendor setup).
- Production (expected >$50k/year): procurement requires a PO and standard vendor onboarding (W-9, vendor form, COI if required).
- Payment terms: typically Net30 for POs. Cards are immediate but preferred for small dollar pilots.

I've attached our vendor_form (FinOpsCo_vendor_form.docx) — please pre-fill where applicable. Also, we'll need a completed W-9 (or equivalent tax doc) and a copy of your MSA (DocuSign link is fine).

We can do a procurement sync next Wednesday (3/24) morning or Thursday (3/25) afternoon PT. Which works for you?

Thanks,
Sarah Chen
Head of Procurement | FinOpsCo
sarah.chen@finopsco.com

Looping in from legal/procurement on our side — happy to run point on the PO/MSA path. A few notes so procurement has visibility: 

- We can provide W-9 and standard MSA via DocuSign today.
- Typical PO onboarding timeline on our side is 2-4 weeks for standard customers once we receive a completed vendor form and PO template. Complex enterprise checks (security questionnaire, custom terms) can extend that to 4-6 weeks.
- If FinOpsCo prefers marketplace for the pilot, we will prioritize enabling the listing. Marketplace removes vendor setup friction but creates different billing flows (we'll share details).

Next actions from Redwood (will do today):
- Marissa: send pre-filled vendor form + W-9 + link to DocuSign MSA (expected EOD).
